matched: Pilot-scale MBR installed in Brazilian oil refinery and monitored for 4 years
Unit configuration: biological tank with submerged flat sheet PES membrane module (Kubota) (Fig. 1)
Pretreatment steps: water-oil separation, flotation, sand filtering, H2O2 dosing for sulphide control
MBR characteristics and operating conditions presented in Table 1
Hydrostatic pressure of water column acts as driving force for permeation
Aeration system provides oxygen for biological process and controls fouling via bubble shear stress
Permeate flow maintained with 1 min relaxation after every 9 min permeation
Chemical recovery cleaning: 5000 mg/L NaClO for 24 h when permeate flow cannot be maintained at maximum hydrostatic pressure

Periodic monitoring parameters: operating conditions (TMP, temp, flowrate, permeability, SRT, pH), sludge characteristics (MLVSS, MLSS, filterability, sedimentability, EPS, SMP), feed/effluent characteristics (BOD, COD, TOC, alkalinity, ammonia, chloride, sulphide, phosphorous, OG, turbidity, color, conductivity)
Measurement methods: Standard Methods [37], Kubota Filter Test (50 mL sludge filtered through folded Whatman 42 paper, initial 5 min volume), membrane permeability calculation
MBR pollutants removal performance presented in Table 2
Removal efficiencies consistent with published literature for pilot-scale MBR treating oil refinery wastewater [38, 39]
